newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader vows to stick to controversial poll.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader vows to stick to controversial poll.

text.p: Hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko stormed out of parliament on Friday after clashing with his opponents and vowed to press ahead with a referendum that he hopes will give him 10 more years in power.
The 41-year-old leader, who has been accused by critics of taking an increasingly authoritarian line, said he had withdrawn proposals intended to appease deputies opposed to the poll.
He reaffirmed his resolve to go ahead with the referendum on a new constitution which would give him a new five-year tenure into the next century.
Lukashenko, who has been in power for two years, says he is confident he would then go on to secure a second five-year term in power.
"I do not see any opportunity to find a compromise in this parliament," Lukashenko said.
Lukashenko took a tough line after the head of the constitutional court warned in parliament that the new constitution, if supported in a referendum, could lead to establishment of a dictatorship.
"Tomorrow we will have a totalitarian regime in the centre of Europe, with the castration of our parliament and the constitutional court," Valery Tikhinya said.
"We, the Constitutional Court, do not have the right to stay silent in this extreme situation," Tikhinya said.
He added that Lukashenko's constitutional project had divided the nation into groups for and against his constitution.

Lukashenko, who has suspended trade unions, closed newspapers and effectively halted market reforms since being elected first post-Soviet president in 1994, said he was withdrawing his offer of compromise to his opponents.
"I will go directly to the people and I will withdraw my initiative, and the people will be our judge," he added.

Lukashenko, who frequently addresses Belarus's 10 million people at length on state television, said he would go ahead with an "All-Belarussian Meeting" on October 19 to seek backing for his plebiscite.
The referendum on the constitution is scheduled for November 7, the anniversary of the 1917 Bolshevik revolution.
Lukashenko had held out an olive branch on Thursday by offering deputies wider powers if they shelved plans for a separate referendum on their own proposed constitution.
Their poll would abolish the post of president altogether.
Some 200 people were jailed for demonstrating against Lukashenko's April pact for creating a "community" with Russia.
Lukashenko has said that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had expressed support for his planned referendum.
Opposition members say Lukashenko's planned October 19 meeting will be attended only by loyal apparatchiks.
